note: The two portfolio content types, taking the space from 11 types to 13.
AWK-31. Read by migrate_portfolio.py, asserted by portfolio-schema.test.ts.
Counted that way ON PURPOSE. AWK-31 calls these 'the twelfth and thirteenth',
but ADR-0012 calls `recording` 'the twelfth content type in the space' — two
accepted claims on slot twelve, because both were written against an 11-type
space and neither anticipated the other landing first. These two landed, so
`recording` will be the FOURTEENTH. Ordinals are the fragile way to say this.
Each entry under `fields` is a VERBATIM Contentful field object, so the applier
sends it as-is and never translates. Anything that is not a field object lives
at the group level, outside them. Same convention as archive-schema.json.
CREATION, not migration. `/projects` is 100% greenfield — no project or
case-study type has ever existed in this space — so unlike archive-schema.json
this file declares whole types, and its required fields are safe because the
types have no entries. The applier will NOT append a required field to a type
that already holds entries; see migrate_portfolio.py.
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. `imageGroup` comes first because `project.body`
restricts its embedded blocks to `imageGroup` by id, and Contentful rejects a
linkContentType naming a type that does not exist. Creating `project` first
fails the migration on its first write. Do not sort this array.
Entries take Contentful's AUTO-GENERATED ids. The archive's `cmp-`/`cnc-`/
`wrk-`/`pi-` ids exist only because import_to_contentful.py computes them;
projects are authored by hand, so they need no prefix convention at all.

layout: ADR-0003's three, verbatim including the camelCase: `sideBySide`, `grid`,
`fullWidth`. These are stored values a component switches on, not display
strings, which is why they are not Title Case like `period` and `forms`.

createTypes.name: Image group
createTypes.description: An ordered set of assets with a layout hint, embedded in a project's body. Captions and alt text come from each Asset, not from here.

createTypes.name: Project
createTypes.description: A piece of design or development work presented at /projects. An empty body means the project is listed in the index and has no page of its own.

richTextNotes: `paragraph` and `text` are deliberately absent from `enabledNodeTypes`, and
that does NOT forbid paragraphs. They are structural nodes, always permitted,
and outside the toggleable set — verified against a content type authored in
the Contentful web app, whose full set is the list above plus
`embedded-entry-inline`.
`embedded-entry-inline` IS dropped, and it is the only place this file trims
Contentful's default. The `nodes` validation constrains embedded-entry-BLOCK
only, so leaving the inline variant enabled would let an author inline-embed
any entry in the space — a concert, a work, a composer — into a case study,
and 'embedded blocks restricted to imageGroup and assets' would be false.
Resource nodes (`embedded-resource-block`/`-inline`, `resource-hyperlink`)
address entries in OTHER spaces. This space has one environment and no
siblings, so they are surfaces with nothing legitimate behind them.
KNOWN GAP, deliberately left open: `entry-hyperlink` and `asset-hyperlink`
stay enabled, which lets body text hyperlink to any entry in the space. A
hyperlink is not an embedded block, so ADR-0003's restriction does not reach
it, and cross-linking a case study to an archive page is plausibly wanted. But
AWK-39's RichText renderer must resolve such a link to a URL or emit a dead
href — there is no schema constraint stopping a link to an entry type the
renderer knows nothing about. Restrict it here if that turns out to be
unwanted; do not discover it in a rendered page.
Marks are NOT trimmed. ADR-0003 restricts embedded blocks and says nothing
about formatting, so narrowing them would be this file inventing an editorial
policy no record decided.

why: `layout: sideBySide` means exactly two images and the other two layouts mean
N, but a Contentful array's size min/max cannot depend on another field's
value. A `max: 2` on `images` would cap `grid` and `fullWidth` too — the
wizard item alone needs five.
So `images` carries NO size validation at all, and the consequence is
permanent: the sideBySide component must tolerate N forever, however AWK-39's
assertion is written. An assertion catches bad data at build time; it does
not stop a three-asset sideBySide group existing in the space.
The fourth invariant Contentful cannot hold, after `sideBySide`'s image
count, `satOut`'s subset rule and `(composer, slug)`'s scoped uniqueness.
Both fields are independently optional and must stay that way — three of the
five entries AWK-21 ships are index-only, so requiring `body` breaks them,
and `featuredRank` is unset on all three. But a featured project with no
`body` has no page, so its home-page card either does not click at all or
clicks off-site to `liveUrl` while the card beside it opens a case study.
That is on the front door, where 2-3 cards carry the whole positioning.
SECOND HALF, recorded under AWK-31 because the schema does not deliver what
ADR-0003 claims for it. The record chose one nullable `featuredRank` over a
boolean plus an order integer 'so the contradictory state does not exist' —
but nothing stops two projects both being rank 1, which reintroduces exactly
the non-deterministic home-page order the record rejected a bare boolean for.
`unique: true` on `featuredRank` was considered and NOT applied: swapping
ranks 1 and 2 transiently needs a duplicate, and Contentful would block the
publish, which is a real cost on a 2-3 item list edited by hand. Assert
distinctness in the build instead, alongside the requires-body rule.
